mainTopic: The end of the story of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, and the משנה about the reminders before שבת and the laws of ספק חשכה: עירוב and טמינה
overview: The amud opens with the end of the story of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in טבריה. He checks the ground, declares hard ground טהור, and marks soft ground, so that כהנים can walk through the marketplace. An elder mocks him, and רבי שמעון rebukes him for undermining a decision he took part in. The story ends with the elder and יהודה בן גרים punished. Then a new משנה teaches that just before שבת a person asks his household about מעשר and עירוב and tells them to light the candle, and it lists what may and may not be done during ספק חשכה. The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source, and adds that these reminders must be said gently. Next, the גמרא resolves a contradiction in the משנה by separating עירובי תחומין from the more lenient עירובי חצרות. רבא's ruling on two עירובין at twilight is defended with the rule סְפֵקָא דְרַבָּנַן לְקוּלָּא. Finally, רבא explains why insulating food is forbidden only after dark, answers אביי's challenge, and begins another teaching that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The priests' problem and רבי שמעון's question
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים had to take a long way around a place of doubtful impurity. רבי שמעון asks whether anyone remembers that this spot was ever considered pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The priests were bothered because they had to walk around that place. רבי שמעון asked: Does anyone know that this place was ever established as pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי wants to fix a problem in טבריה, so he asks the townspeople for information. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People suspected a dead body might be buried in the area, so כהנים, who may not become טמא from a corpse, avoided it. רבי שמעון wants a starting point. If the place once had a חזקה of purity, he can build on that.

keyTerms.meaning: To go around, take a detour

phrases.english: And they had trouble
for the priests, to go around it.
He said: Is there a person
who knows that purity was ever established here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous דף about רבי שמעון wanting to improve טבריה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether anyone knows of a past חזקה of טהרה for this area

steps.title: An elder remembers רבן יוחנן בן זכאי planting there
steps.stepSummary: An elder testifies that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, a כהן, once grew and cut lupines of תרומה in this very place.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: Here בן זכאי cut lupines of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone answers רבי שמעון's question. An old man remembers that this spot was once treated as pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה must be handled in purity, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was a כהן. So if he grew and harvested תרומה here, at least part of this place must have been considered טהור. That gives רבי שמעון the starting point he needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
Here ben Zakkai cut
lupines of teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The place was once treated as pure, because רבן יוחנן בן זכאי harvested תרומה there

steps.title: רבי שמעון checks the ground and purifies it
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון examines the ground. Where it is hard he declares it pure, and where it is soft he marks it as possibly impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also did the same. Every place that was hard, he declared pure. Every place that was soft, he marked.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון acts on the information and goes through the area to clear the safe spots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hard ground means it was never dug up, so no body is buried there, and that spot is טהור. Soft ground may hide a grave, so he marks it as a warning. Now כהנים can walk through the marketplace safely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This was the תקנה רבי שמעון made for the city, like יעקב who improved the city he came to. It is the act the elder will now mock.

phrases.english: He too did so:
everywhere that was hard, he declared it pure,
and everywhere that was soft, he marked it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Acts on the testimony of the elder
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hard ground is declared טהור and soft ground is marked as possibly טמא

steps.title: An elder mocks רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: An elder mockingly says that בן יוחי purified a cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said: בן יוחי purified the cemetery!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks what רבי שמעון just did. This sets up רבי שמעון's angry response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elder makes it sound as if רבי שמעון declared a real בית הקברות to be טהור, which would be shocking. In fact, רבי שמעון only cleared spots that were checked and found safe. The elder's remark is ridicule more than a real legal argument.

phrases.english: A certain elder said:
Ben Yoḥai purified the cemetery!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action of step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's purification of the area
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mocks the act as if a known cemetery had been declared pure

steps.title: רבי שמעון rebukes the elder for breaking ranks
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the elder could have objected if he had not been part of the decision. But since he was counted among those who decided, mocking it now makes תלמידי חכמים look worse than harlots, who at least help each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you had not been with us, or even if you were with us but not counted with us, you would be speaking fairly. Now that you were with us and counted with us, people will say: harlots do each other's makeup, so all the more so תלמידי חכמים should support each other!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון rejects the elder's mockery. He does not argue about purity itself. He attacks the elder for undermining a decision he took part in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An outsider who disagreed would have a fair complaint. But the elder was part of the group that voted, so mocking the decision afterward is disloyal. The קל וחומר: even rival harlots help each other look good, so תלמידי חכמים should certainly stand behind each other.

keyTerms.meaning: If only, had it been that
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say the elder is wrong about the facts. His complaint is that the elder publicly undermined a group decision he was part of.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Had you not been with us,
and even had you been with us

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נִמְנֵיתָ עִמָּנוּ — יָפֶה אַתָּה אוֹמֵר.
phrases.english: but were not counted with us, you would speak well.
Now that you were with us and were counted with us,

phrases.aramaic: יֹאמְרוּ: זוֹנוֹת מְפַרְכְּסוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ,
phrases.english: people will say: harlots apply makeup to one another,
Torah scholars, all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mockery of step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the elder's right to mock, not the facts
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elder was part of the decision and is now publicly undermining it

steps.title: The elder and יהודה בן גרים are punished
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון looks at the elder and he dies. Then he sees יהודה בן גרים, whose gossip started the whole affair, and turns him into a pile of bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He set his eyes on him, and he died. He went out to the market and saw יהודה בן גרים. He said: Does this one still exist in the world? He set his eyes on him and made him a pile of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי שמעון punishing both the mocking elder and יהודה בן גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה בן גרים had repeated רבי שמעון's words to the government, which caused his years of hiding. Seeing him still alive, רבי שמעון punishes him. This closes the long אגדה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי purified טבריה by checking hard and soft ground. He strongly defended the unity of חכמים, and the story ends with יהודה בן גרים punished.

phrases.english: He set his eyes on him, and he died.

phrases.aramaic: נְפַק לְשׁוּקָא חַזְיֵיהּ לִיהוּדָה בֶּן גֵּרִים.
phrases.english: He went out to the market and saw Yehuda ben Gerim.
He said: Does this one still exist in the world?
He set his eyes on him
and made him into a pile of bones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story after the rebuke
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי ends with the punishment of those who opposed him

steps.title: The three questions before שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: right before nightfall on ערב שבת, a person must ask his household whether they took מעשר and made an עירוב, and then tell them to light the candle.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person must say three things in his home on ערב שבת as it gets dark: Did you tithe? Did you make the עירוב? Light the candle.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: the reminders a person gives his household just before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once שבת starts, a person can no longer take מעשר, make an עירוב, or light candles. So at the last moment he checks that the first two are done and then has the candle lit. The משנה says this is said עם חשכה, close to dark, when the reminder is most needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)

phrases.english: MISHNA: Three things
a person must say in his home
on Shabbat eve as it gets dark:
Have you tithed? Have you made the eiruv?
Light the lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים צָרִיךְ אָדָם לוֹמַר בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; unrelated to the preceding אגדה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before שבת one must check on מעשר and עירוב and then have the candle lit

steps.title: What may and may not be done at twilight
steps.stepSummary: During ספק חשכה, one may not tithe certainly untithed produce, immerse vessels, or light candles. One may tithe דמאי, make an עירוב, and insulate hot food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is doubtful whether it is dark or not yet dark: we do not tithe definitely untithed produce, we do not immerse vessels, and we do not light candles. But we may tithe דמאי, make an עירוב, and insulate hot water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with rules for the doubtful twilight period, sorting actions into forbidden and permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden acts are stricter matters: tithing וודאי is like a real תיקון, and lighting is a full מלאכה. The permitted acts are lighter: דמאי is only a doubtful obligation from the חכמים, and an עירוב and insulating food are rabbinic matters. The חכמים allowed these lighter acts during a time that might still be day.

keyTerms.meaning: Doubtful whether it is already dark (twilight)
Produce that was definitely not tithed
Produce of doubtful tithing status, bought from an עם הארץ
Insulate the hot food or water

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ודאי and דמאי. ודאי was definitely not tithed and may not be tithed now. דמאי is only doubtful and may still be tithed at twilight.
steps.whatToRemember: At twilight: no tithing of ודאי, no immersing vessels, no lighting. But tithing דמאי, making an עירוב, and insulating hot food are allowed.

phrases.english: If it is uncertain whether it is dark or not dark,
one may not tithe definitely untithed produce,
and one may not immerse vessels,
and one may not light the lamps.
But one may tithe demai,
and make an eiruv, and insulate the hot food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with rules for twilight
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stricter acts are forbidden at twilight; lighter rabbinic acts are permitted

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the rule of the three reminders comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for a source for the משנה's first rule. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the obligation to speak to one's household before שבת. It is not about the specific twilight laws.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (marks the start of the discussion)
From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's first rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the obligation to remind one's household before שבת

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי brings a פסוק from איוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי cites a פסוק: "You will know your tent is at peace; you will visit your home and not sin."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The פסוק says: "And you shall know that your tent is in peace, and you shall visit your habitation, and shall not sin."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a פסוק that hints at checking on one's home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Visit your habitation" is read as checking up on your household. "And shall not sin" shows the purpose: making sure no חטא, such as eating untithed food or carrying without an עירוב, happens on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall visit (check) your home

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The verse said:
"And you shall know that your tent is in peace,
and you shall visit your habitation, and shall not sin."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in איוב: check on your home so that you will not sin

steps.title: Say the reminders gently
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא teaches that although one must say these three things, he must say them calmly so the household will accept them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Even though the חכמים said a person must say three things, he must say them gently, so that they will accept them from him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching adds how the reminders must be said: gently, not harshly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said what to ask. רבה בר רב הונא adds the manner. If a person asks harshly before שבת, his family may be afraid and answer falsely, which could lead to sin. Speaking calmly makes them listen and tell the truth.

keyTerms.meaning: So that they will accept them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical lesson for every ערב שבת: the right tone is part of keeping the home free of sin.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Even though the Rabbis said

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים צָרִיךְ אָדָם לוֹמַר וְכוּ׳ —
phrases.english: three things a person must say, etc.,
he must say them calmly,
so that they will accept them from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the manner of fulfilling the משנה's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three reminders must be said gently so they will be accepted

steps.title: רב אשי reached the same idea by reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says he never heard רבה בר רב הונא's teaching but already practiced it based on his own logic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I did not hear this teaching of רבה בר רב הונא, but I fulfilled it on my own based on reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a personal note confirming רבה בר רב הונא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law. רב אשי shows the teaching is so logical that a wise person reaches it on his own. This supports רבה בר רב הונא's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for the three reminders is "וּפָקַדְתָּ נָוְךָ וְלֹא תֶחֱטָא." They must be said gently, and רב אשי confirms this is simple common sense.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I did not hear
this teaching of Rabba bar Rav Huna,
but I fulfilled it from reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי הָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms step 11 through independent reasoning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking gently is logically required, even without a received tradition

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself about making an עירוב at dusk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the beginning of the משנה implies you cannot make an עירוב during ספק חשכה, while the later part says you can.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה itself is difficult. You said: 'Three things a person must say in his home on ערב שבת עם חשכה.' That means close to nightfall, yes, but during ספק חשכה, no. Then the משנה teaches: 'During ספק חשכה, one may make an עירוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the first half of the משנה against the second half and says they clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase עם חשכה means 'just before dark,' while it is still surely day. That implies that once it is ספק חשכה, it is too late to ask 'did you make the עירוב?', because nothing can be done anymore. Yet the end of the משנה explicitly allows making an עירוב during ספק חשכה.

keyTerms.meaning: This [teaching] itself is difficult, meaning it contradicts itself internally
Close to nightfall, while it is still definitely day
Doubtful dark: it is unclear whether night has started
And then it teaches, introducing a later clause of the same source

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not between two different sources. Both lines come from the same משנה, which is why the גמרא says גופא, 'itself.'

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: three things
a person must say in his home
on Friday close to nightfall.
Close to nightfall, yes;
phrases.notes: Read it as: only while it's still definitely day.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק חֲשֵׁכָה סָפֵק אֵינוֹ חֲשֵׁכָה — לָא.
phrases.english: when it is unclear whether it is dark or not dark, no.
And then it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק חֲשֵׁכָה סָפֵק אֵינוֹ חֲשֵׁכָה — מְעָרֵב.
phrases.english: When it is unclear whether it is dark or not dark, one may make an eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion on the reminders (steps 9-12) to the משנה's text and finds an internal contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two clauses of the משנה: the three reminders עם חשכה versus מערבין during ספק חשכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inferring from 'עם חשכה' that ספק חשכה is too late for an עירוב contradicts the explicit later ruling that one may make an עירוב during ספק חשכה.

steps.title: A memory aid listing רב's teachings in this chain
steps.stepSummary: Before giving the answer, the גמרא inserts a סימן, a mnemonic of key words for a series of teachings by the same chain of אמוראים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mnemonic: 'In itself,' 'pruning,' 'bird,' 'in a cord of silk.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is an aside, not part of the argument. The גמרא gives a memory aid before stating the answer, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word reminds the student of a different teaching that רבי אבא said in the name of רב חייא בר אשי, quoting רב, in מסכת שבת. The first word, בגופיא, points to this very answer about the משנה contradicting 'itself' (גופא).

keyTerms.meaning: 'In itself', hinting at the current answer to הא גופא קשיא
Pruning, a hint to another teaching of this chain
A bird, a hint to another teaching
A cord of silk/fine wool, a hint to another teaching

phrases.english: Mnemonic:
in itself, pruning, bird,
in a cord of silk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interrupts between the question and its answer to list the answering chain's teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory aid for a series of teachings by רבי אבא, citing רב חייא בר אשי, quoting רב.

steps.title: Two different kinds of עירוב: boundaries versus courtyards
steps.stepSummary: רב resolves the contradiction: the strict first clause refers to עירובי תחומין, and the lenient second clause refers to עירובי חצרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב חייא בר אשי, quoting רב: It is not difficult. Here, the משנה is speaking about עירובי תחומין. There, it is speaking about עירובי חצרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the contradiction by saying each half of the משנה is talking about a different type of עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירובי תחומין extends how far one may walk on שבת and is treated more strictly, so it must be made while it is surely day. That is why the reminder must come עם חשכה. עירובי חצרות allows carrying between courtyards and is more lenient, so it may still be made during ספק חשכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the standard opening of an answer
Here... here: each clause refers to a different case
An עירוב that extends one's walking boundary on שבת
An עירוב that joins courtyards so one may carry between them

steps.whatToRemember: Strict about time: עירובי תחומין, which must be made while it is surely day. Lenient: עירובי חצרות, which may be made even during ספק חשכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Both are called עירוב, but they are completely different mechanisms with different rules. Do not mix them up.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
It is not difficult:
here it refers to joining of boundaries,
here it refers to joining of courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּעֵירוּבֵי תְּחוּמִין, כָּאן בְּעֵירוּבֵי חֲצֵרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each clause refers to a different type of עירוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses refer to the same kind of עירוב, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The early cutoff applies to עירובי תחומין; permission during ספק חשכה applies to the more lenient עירובי חצרות.

steps.title: רבא's case: two עירובי חצרות, both valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that even when timing is doubtful at both ends, an עירובי חצרות still works, which shows how lenient it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Two people told someone, 'Go make an עירוב for us.' For one he made it while it was still day, and for the other he made it during בין השמשות. The one made by day was eaten during בין השמשות, and the one made during בין השמשות was eaten after dark. Both of them acquired the עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ruling by רבא that shows how lenient the rules of עירובי חצרות are when the timing is doubtful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב works only if it exists at the moment שבת begins, and בין השמשות is a time of doubt. For the first person, maybe שבת had already begun before the food was eaten, and for the second, maybe it was still day when it was placed. Each case is a doubt, and since עירובי חצרות is lenient, the doubt is decided in favor of validity, so both people acquired the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight: the uncertain period between day and night
They acquired the עירוב, meaning it took effect for them

steps.whyThisMatters: It supports רב's answer: עירובי חצרות is lenient enough that doubts about בין השמשות do not cancel it.
steps.whatToRemember: With עירובי חצרות, a doubt about whether the עירוב existed when שבת began is resolved leniently.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Two people said to him:
Go and make an eruv for us.
For one he made the eruv while it was still day,
and for one he made the eruv at twilight.
The one for whom he made it while still day
had his eruv eaten at twilight,
and the one for whom he made it at twilight
had his eruv eaten after dark.
Both of them acquired the eruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: אָמְרוּ לוֹ שְׁנַיִם צֵא וְעָרֵב עָלֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling showing the leniency of עירובי חצרות at twilight, in line with רב's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירובי חצרות is valid even when it was eaten during בין השמשות, or placed during בין השמשות and eaten after dark. Both people acquire the עירוב.

steps.title: Twilight cannot be both day and night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling. If בין השמשות is day, only the second case should work. If it is night, only the first case should work. Both cannot work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way you look at it, there is a problem! If twilight is day, the latter one should acquire his עירוב and the first one should not. And if twilight is night, the first one should acquire and the latter one should not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's statement from the last step, which said an עירוב works in both twilight cases. It shows that these two cases seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the עירוב was eaten during twilight. That only works if twilight counts as night, so that שבת had already started while the food still existed. In the second case, the עירוב was placed during twilight. That only works if twilight counts as day, so that the food was set out before שבת. Twilight cannot be treated as night for one case and as day for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it; an 'either way' challenge
Twilight, the in-between time after sunset
Let him acquire, meaning the עירוב takes effect for him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which case is which. 'The first one' (קמא) is the case where the עירוב was eaten at twilight. 'The latter one' (בתרא) is the case where the עירוב was placed at twilight.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to look at both possibilities, and either way there's a problem.

phrases.english: If twilight is day,
let the latter one acquire,
phrases.notes: The one who placed his עירוב at twilight; it was placed while still 'day'

phrases.english: but let the first one not acquire.
phrases.notes: His עירוב was eaten while it was still 'day'

phrases.english: And if twilight is night,
let the first one acquire,
phrases.notes: His עירוב still existed when שבת began

phrases.english: but let the latter one not acquire!
phrases.notes: His עירוב was placed only after שבת had started

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the עירוב works in both twilight cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each case needs twilight to have the opposite status, so ruling both valid is logically inconsistent.

steps.title: Twilight is a doubt, so we are lenient
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the status of בין השמשות is uncertain, and a doubt in a rabbinic law is ruled leniently. So both cases work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Twilight is a doubt, and a doubt in a rabbinic law is ruled leniently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. We do not decide whether twilight is day or night; we treat it as a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירובי חצרות is a rabbinic law. With a rabbinic doubt, we are allowed to rule leniently in each case on its own. So we may be lenient in both cases, even though that seems inconsistent, because neither case is ever ruled 'definitely day' or 'definitely night.'

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt in a rabbinic law is ruled leniently

steps.whatToRemember: בין השמשות is a ספק. For a rabbinic law like עירובי חצרות, we are lenient whichever way the doubt could fall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule found all over the תלמוד: סְפֵקָא דְרַבָּנַן לְקוּלָּא. It explains why the lenient side wins in רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: Twilight is a doubt,
and a doubt in a rabbinic matter is ruled leniently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes twilight as a doubt rather than a fixed status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Twilight must be definitely day or definitely night, so only one case could work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Twilight is a ספק. Since עירובי חצרות is rabbinic, we rule leniently in both cases.

steps.title: Why insulating is forbidden after dark
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why the חכמים forbade insulating food after nightfall, even in something that does not add heat. They feared a person might come to reboil the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why did they say that one may not insulate food, even in something that does not add heat, once it is dark? It is a decree, lest he come to boil it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the משנה's last clause, which allows insulating hot food at twilight. רבא explains why insulating (טמינה) is forbidden once it is definitely dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Insulating in something that does not add heat only keeps the food warm, so it seems harmless. רבא says it was still forbidden after dark. The concern is that by then the food may have cooled, and the person might put it back on the fire to boil it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Insulate or wrap food to keep it warm
From when it gets dark (Shabbat has begun)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about insulating in something that adds heat; that is forbidden even before שבת. This rule is about something that only keeps existing heat in, and it is forbidden only after dark.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Why did they say
one may not insulate in something
that does not add heat
from nightfall?
It is a decree, lest he boil it.
phrases.notes: He might reheat the cooled food on שבת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the last clause of the משנה (step 8), 'וטומנין את החמין' at twilight, and explains why insulating is forbidden once it is definitely dark
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on insulating, even in something that adds no heat, after dark is a גזירה that one might reboil the food.

steps.title: אביי asks why the decree does not apply at twilight
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: if the worry is reboiling, the חכמים should also forbid insulating during בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, we should also make the decree during twilight!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's reason. He says the same worry should forbid insulating during twilight too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows insulating during בין השמשות. If the worry is that someone might come to boil the food, that worry exists at twilight as well. So רבא's reason seems to forbid too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reasoning is correct

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so,
during twilight we should also decree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reason in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason (שמא ירתיח) for the ban after dark
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry about reboiling applies equally at twilight, yet insulating is allowed then.

steps.title: Pots are usually still boiling at twilight
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that at twilight, pots are usually still boiling hot, so there is no reason to worry that someone will reboil them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Ordinary pots are boiling hot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge by pointing out how things normally are at twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At twilight, the pots were just taken off the fire and are still boiling, so nobody needs to reheat them. Only later at night do they cool down, and then the fear of reboiling begins. That is why the decree starts from nightfall.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on insulating after dark is a גזירה against reboiling. It does not apply at twilight, because pots are normally still boiling then.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Ordinary pots are boiling.
phrases.notes: At twilight they were just removed from the fire

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סְתָם קְדֵירוֹת רוֹתְחוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by the usual real-world situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry about reboiling should apply at twilight too.
steps.terutzMaskana: At twilight pots are usually still boiling, so there is no worry about reboiling; the decree applies only after dark.

steps.title: Another teaching of רבא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces another statement of רבא, which continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. It introduces a new teaching of רבא, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'And' (ו) ties this new teaching to the previous ones, so it is part of the same series of רבא's teachings. The actual content comes in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבא said; introduces another statement by the same Amora

phrases.english: And Rava said:
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next עמוד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Setup line for a new teaching in the same series of רבא's teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction only; the ruling follows on the next amud.
